stones__blue-aventurine.colors: Aventurine is most often green; blue is named as one of the other, less common colors.

stones__blue-jade.colors: Jade comes in many colors including blue. S3 lists blue among jadeite colors.

stones__chalcocite.colors: Dark gray to black, per S1.

stones__dalmatian-jasper.colors: White to cream base with black spots; S4 adds brown spots. Spots rarely exceed 4 mm.

stones__dumortierite.colors: Brown, blue and green are most common; violet and pink are rarer.

stones__goethite.colors: Yellowish to reddish to dark brown or black.

stones__green-onyx.colors: Onyx is black and white banded, and sardonyx is red to brown with black or white. Green onyx is usually dyed green chalcedony, and chrysoprase is apple green chalcedony.

stones__green-tourmaline.colors: Green tourmaline is dark green, sometimes light green or light brown.

stones__honey-calcite.colors: Pure calcite is colorless or white. When colored crystals are found, they are generally yellow to honey-colored, per S5.

stones__iris-agate.colors: Base color light grey to brown; iridescent colors include blue, green, purple and yellow (per S5).

stones__kambaba-jasper.colors: Green, with blackish, irregularly shaped orbs.

stones__kingman-turquoise.colors: Medium to dark blue with pyrite flecks; bright blue with black spider-web matrix per S3. Turquoise overall runs blue to green.

stones__labradorite.colors: Body color usually clear, white or gray; labradorescent flashes of blue, green, yellow, orange and red.

stones__laguna-agate.colors: Laguna hues run from reds and oranges to yellows, pinks and purples, framed by whites and grays, per S4.

stones__larvikite.colors: Black, blue, brown, gray and white per S2, with a silver-blue sheen on polished surfaces.

stones__lavender-jade.colors: Jadeite occurs in many colors including lavender, lilac, pink, green and white.

stones__lemurian-quartz.colors: Usually sold as clear quartz crystals.

stones__libyan-desert-glass.colors: Canary yellow to yellow-green, per S4 and S1.

stones__london-blue-topaz.colors: London blue is a deep blue (S4).

stones__magnetite.colors: Black to silvery gray per S1; black or gray with a brownish tint in reflected sun per S2.

stones__mahogany-obsidian.colors: Deep brown to black with reddish-brown patches, streaks or swirls. The common mix is black and brown swirled together.

stones__merlinite.colors: Black dendrites on a translucent or white background (S3). The host chalcedony is most often white to gray, grayish-blue or brown (S2).

stones__orange-diamond.colors: Orangey-red to yellowish-orange, with pure orange being very rare.

stones__orthoceras.colors: Fossil shows as chambers in white calcite inside a red, pink or grey limestone matrix in the museum specimen (S2).

stones__painite.colors: Deep garnet red to brownish red-orange.

stones__peach-moonstone.colors: Peach ranges from light apricot to rich peach with a silvery or pearly sheen (S5). Moonstone overall spans white, gray, brown, pink, orange, green, yellow and colorless (S3).

stones__pink-amethyst.colors: Lilac to deep reddish purple (S2). Pinkish violet 'Rose de France' is the lightest shade (S2, S4). Most valued is strong reddish purple (S1).

stones__pink-opal.colors: Pale pink, pink and dark red-pink per S7. Peruvian material is pastel pink, often with blue and green stones.

stones__pink-topaz.colors: Topaz occurs in natural colors including pink. Pink is one of the most highly regarded colors (S2).

stones__white-jade.colors: Nephrite usually ranges from white through cream to dark green. Hetian stone runs creamy white to greenish, with pure white the most valuable.

facts.abalone-shell: The iridescent inner lining of abalone shells is nacre, also called mother-of-pearl, a biomineral made by the mollusk.
facts.actinolite: Mineral species in a solid-solution series.
facts.adamite: Mineral species, the zinc member of an adamite-olivenite series with the copper analogue olivenite.
facts.adularia: Adularia is a white or colorless, transparent to translucent variety of orthoclase, the feldspar behind moonstone's sheen.
facts.aegirine: Aegirine is a sodium iron pyroxene mineral, known for long slender crystals with distinctive terminations that collectors prize.
facts.afghanite: A rare blue mineral first identified in 1968, named after Afghanistan.
facts.agate: A translucent, usually banded variety of microcrystalline quartz (fibrous chalcedony), used as a semiprecious stone.
facts.agatized-coral: Agatized coral is silicified coral from the Ballast Point area of Tampa Bay, Florida, made into jewelry and ornaments.
facts.ajoite: Ajoite is a copper silicate mineral named for its type locality at Ajo, Arizona.
facts.alabandite: Alabandite is an uncommon sulfide mineral with a fairly simple chemical formula.
facts.albite: Albite is the sodium end member of the plagioclase feldspar series, usually white, with a few small gems cut from it.
facts.alexandrite: The very rare color-change variety of the mineral chrysoberyl.
facts.allophane: Allophane is a translucent, apparently amorphous mineral that forms crusts, masses and stalactites.
facts.almandine: Almandine is the most common member of the garnet group and the garnet most widely faceted for jewelry.
facts.alunite: Alunite is a potassium aluminum sulfate mineral of the alunite group that forms where sulfate reacts with aluminous rocks.
facts.alurgite: Alurgite is a manganese-rich, pink to red variety of the mica mineral muscovite.
facts.amazonite: A green to blue-green color variety of microcline, a potassium feldspar, cut as cabochons and beads.
facts.amber: Fossilized tree resin, an organic gem material.
facts.amblygonite: Amblygonite is the fluorine-dominant member of a mineral series with montebrasite, and is much rarer.
facts.amethyst: The purple color variety of quartz, used in adornment for over 2000 years.
facts.ametrine: Ametrine is a transparent quartz that shows the colors of both amethyst and citrine in a single gem.
facts.ammolite: Gem-quality material made from fossil shells of certain ammonite species, found in Alberta.
facts.analcime: Analcime is a zeolite group mineral that often occurs with other zeolites and is closely related to the feldspathoids.
facts.anapaite: Anapaite is a triclinic mineral of calcium, iron and phosphate with four waters, named after Anapa in Russia.
facts.anatase: Anatase is a relatively uncommon but very aesthetic form of titanium dioxide, polymorphous with rutile and brookite.
facts.andesine: Andesine is a plagioclase feldspar, named for the Andes Mountains, that the IMA treats as a calcium-rich variety of albite.
facts.andradite: Andradite is a member of the garnet group that can be cut into fine gems such as demantoid.
facts.anglesite: Anglesite is a secondary lead mineral that forms through the alteration of lead sulfides, mainly galena.
facts.anhydrite: Anhydrite is an anhydrous calcium sulfate mineral, mostly found in evaporite deposits and the cap rocks above salt domes.
facts.anorthite: Anorthite is the most calcium-rich and sodium-poor plagioclase feldspar, and the rarest of the plagioclases.
facts.anorthoclase: Anorthoclase is the intermediate member of the albite-sanidine feldspar series, found in high-temperature sodium-rich volcanic rocks.
facts.anorthosite: Anorthosite is an igneous rock made of 90 percent or more plagioclase feldspar, often labradorite when used as a gem rock.
facts.anthophyllite: Anthophyllite is an amphibole mineral that forms in medium to high grade metamorphic rocks and is named for its clove color.
facts.antigorite: Antigorite is a magnesium iron silicate mineral of the serpentine group, sometimes dyed and sold as other stones.
facts.antlerite: Antlerite is an uncommon mineral typically formed in the oxidized zone of copper deposits under highly acid conditions.
facts.apatite: A group of calcium phosphate minerals.
facts.apophyllite: A solid solution series of minerals including fluorapophyllite-(K), fluorapophyllite-(Na) and hydroxyapophyllite-(K).
facts.apricot-agate: Apricot Agate is a name for agate nodules in pinkish orange to yellowish orange, often with white banding.
facts.aquamarine: The greenish blue to blue color variety of the mineral beryl.
facts.aquaprase: Aquaprase is the trade name of a bluish green chalcedony, colored by chromium and nickel, from an undisclosed location in Africa.
facts.aragonite: A carbonate mineral, one of the three most common crystal forms of calcium carbonate, and a polymorph of calcite.
facts.argentite: Argentite is the name for the isometric, high temperature form of silver sulfide, now known as acanthite when cooled.
facts.arizona-pietersite: Arizona Pietersite is a marketing name for asbestiform serpentine, a look-alike that is not true pietersite.
facts.arsenopyrite: Arsenopyrite is an iron arsenic sulfide and the most abundant arsenic-bearing mineral.
facts.astrophyllite: Astrophyllite is a mineral of the astrophyllite group, found in nepheline syenites, alkali granites and their pegmatites.
facts.atacamite: Atacamite is a copper chloride hydroxide mineral that forms as an oxidation product of other copper minerals in arid, saline settings.
facts.augite: Augite is the most common pyroxene mineral and a member of the clinopyroxene group, found in mafic igneous rocks.
facts.aurichalcite: Aurichalcite is a fragile zinc and copper mineral with a pastel color that forms in oxidized zones of copper and zinc deposits.
facts.australian-opal: Australian opal is opal from Australia, a sedimentary stone that makes up 95 percent of the world supply.
facts.autunite: Autunite is a radioactive secondary mineral that forms from uranium-bearing minerals.
facts.aventurine: Aventurine is a variety of translucent quartz or quartzite with small flake-shaped inclusions that give it a sparkle.
facts.azurite: A soft, deep-blue copper carbonate mineral from weathered copper ore, used as a gem material, ornamental stone, ore of copper and pigment.
facts.banded-agate: Agate forms when silica from groundwater is deposited in cavities, often in volcanic rock, in concentric or horizontal layers.
facts.banded-amethyst: Banded amethyst is quartz in which purple amethyst bands with white milky quartz and a little gray smoky quartz.
facts.barite: A mineral made of barium sulfate (BaSO4), and the principal source of barium.
facts.bastnasite: Bastnasite is the most abundant rare earth bearing mineral, found in carbonatites, granites and pegmatites.
facts.bauxite: Bauxite is a rock, not a mineral, made mainly of aluminum-bearing minerals and it is the primary ore of aluminum.
facts.benitoite: Benitoite is an extremely rare barium titanium silicate mineral and the official state gemstone of California.
facts.beryl: Beryl is a relatively rare beryllium aluminum silicate mineral whose color varieties include emerald and aquamarine.
facts.beryllonite: Beryllonite is a rare sodium beryllium phosphate mineral that forms in granitic and alkalic pegmatites.
facts.bicolor-tourmaline: Tourmaline with two color zones in one crystal or gem, a pattern tied to growth zoning.
facts.bismuth: Bismuth is an uncommon native element mineral with a metallic silver-white color and a reddish hue.
facts.bismuthinite: Bismuthinite is an uncommon bismuth sulfide mineral and an important ore of bismuth, with interesting crystal habits.
facts.bixbyite: Bixbyite is an uncommon manganese iron oxide mineral known for its dark, lustrous cubic crystals.
facts.black-diamond: Black diamond is a single-crystal diamond made black by dark inclusions, unlike carbonado, which is a polycrystalline diamond aggregate.
facts.black-garnet: Black garnet is melanite, the naturally black variety of andradite garnet.
facts.black-kyanite: Black kyanite is kyanite in black, a less common color than the usual blue of gem kyanite.
facts.black-mica: Black Mica is the name for a group of dark sheet silicate minerals, known as biotite.
facts.black-onyx: Black onyx is mostly dyed black chalcedony, since naturally solid black onyx is rare.
facts.black-quartz: Smoky quartz color comes from natural gamma radiation acting on aluminum impurities.
facts.black-spinel: Spinel is one species in a group of related minerals (spinel subgroup).
facts.black-star-diopside: Black star diopside is naturally black diopside that can show a four-ray star, caused by parallel needle inclusions.
facts.black-star-sapphire: Black star sapphire is a very dark, opaque sapphire whose star effect comes from needle-like inclusions.
facts.bloodstone: A dark green chalcedony with spatters of bright red.
facts.blue-amber: Amber that shows strong blue fluorescence and looks blue on a black background.
facts.blue-aventurine: A blue-colored example of aventurine, a translucent quartz or quartzite with sparkling mica or similar inclusions.
facts.blue-barite: Blue barite is the blue form of barite, a barium sulfate mineral, shown as tabular crystals from Muddy Creek, Colorado.
facts.blue-chalcedony: The blue color variety of chalcedony (cryptocrystalline quartz), prized by carvers and jewelry designers for its ethereal blues.
facts.blue-diamond: Blue diamond is a rare fancy colored diamond whose color mostly comes from trace boron.
facts.blue-halite: Blue halite is halite, the natural form of salt, whose blue color comes from defects in the crystal.
facts.blue-jade: Jadeite colors are caused by impurities.
facts.blue-john-fluorite: Blue John is a massive, banded fluorite, also called Derbyshire spar, mostly from Treak Cliff near Castleton in England.
facts.blue-kyanite: Blue kyanite is the common blue form of kyanite, an aluminum silicate mineral.
facts.blue-moonstone: Moonstone that shows a blue adularescence (blue flash or blue sheen), rare in colorless feldspar.
facts.blue-opal: A common opal with blue body color and no play-of-color, mostly from Peru.
facts.blue-quartz: Dumortierite inclusions color the quartz blue.
facts.blue-spinel: Blue spinel is spinel colored blue, mostly by iron with slight cobalt, while cobalt spinels owe a vivid blue to dominant cobalt.
facts.blue-tigers-eye: Natural blue tiger's eye is hawk's eye, unaltered crocidolite in quartz.
facts.blue-topaz: A color form of topaz, the silicate mineral.
facts.blue-tourmaline: A blue color of tourmaline, a large boron silicate mineral group.
facts.blue-turquoise: Turquoise in its blue color, especially sky or robin's-egg blue, which is the most valued color.
facts.boleite: Boleite is an uncommon blue mineral that forms cubic crystals and is mostly a collector mineral.
facts.boracite: Boracite is a mineral that forms in salt deposits and is rarely cut as a gem.
facts.botryoidal-hematite: The iridescent coating sometimes seen on hematite is attributed to turgite, a mix of hematite and goethite.
facts.boulder-opal: A gem made of precious opal within or attached to its natural host rock.
facts.bowenite: Bowenite is a translucent, fine-grained variety of antigorite, a serpentine mineral, used as a jade substitute and for carving.
facts.brazilianite: Brazilianite is a hydrothermal mineral that forms in phosphate-rich zones of granite pegmatites.
facts.brochantite: Brochantite is a secondary copper mineral that forms in the oxidation zone of copper deposits, and it is a minor copper ore.
facts.brookite: A titanium dioxide (TiO2) mineral, the orthorhombic form of TiO2, and one of three main forms of titanium dioxide.
facts.brown-diamond: Brown diamonds are the most common natural fancy colored diamonds and come in hues from champagne to cognac.
facts.brucite: Brucite is a mineral used industrially as a magnesium ore.
facts.buddstone: Buddstone is a bright green variety of chalcedony colored by abundant inclusions of fuchsite mica.
facts.bumblebee-jasper: Bright yellow-to-orange and black patterned gem from West Java, Indonesia.
facts.burmese-jade: Burmese jade is jadeite jade from the mines in Mogaung, Upper Burma, now Myanmar.
facts.bustamite: Bustamite is a mineral between the rhodonite and wollastonite series, classed as its own mineral and not a variety.
facts.bytownite: Bytownite is a calcium-rich member of the plagioclase feldspar series, and transparent crystals are rare.
facts.cacoxenite: Cacoxenite is a mineral that is a common accessory in oxidized magnetite and limonite iron ores.
facts.calcite: A very common rock-forming carbonate mineral, CaCO3, and the main mineral of limestone and marble.
facts.canasite: Canasite is a monoclinic calcium, sodium and potassium silicate mineral from the Khibiny and Murun massifs in Russia.
facts.cancrinite: Cancrinite is a mineral of alkali-rich rocks that is sometimes cut as opaque to translucent gem material.
facts.carnelian: A translucent orange to red to brown variety of chalcedony, colored by iron.
facts.cassiterite: Mineral species of the rutile group, an oxide.
facts.cats-eye-jade: Nephrite, a jade, with a chatoyant cat's eye effect.
facts.cavansite: Cavansite is a calcium vanadium silicate mineral, first described from Oregon and dimorphous with pentagonite.
facts.celestite: A strontium sulfate mineral, also called celestine, named from Latin for heavenly because of its often sky-blue color.
facts.ceruleite: Ceruleite is a rare sky-blue mineral that forms in the oxidized zone of arsenic-rich ore deposits.
facts.cerussite: Lead carbonate mineral and an important lead ore.
facts.chabazite: Chabazite is a series of related zeolite minerals, mostly kept as collector specimens.
facts.chalcanthite: Chalcanthite is a water-soluble secondary copper mineral formed by the oxidation of copper sulfides.
facts.chalcopyrite: Chalcopyrite is a brass yellow copper iron sulfide mineral and the most important ore of copper.
facts.charoite: A purple ornamental gem material that is really a rock, almost purely made of the mineral charoite.
facts.chicken-blood-stone: Rock (a mix of minerals), not a mineral species.
facts.chinese-writing-stone: Chinese writing stone is a name for what appears to be a basalt porphyry, with light feldspar crystals in a dark groundmass.
facts.chondrodite: Chondrodite is the best known member of the humite group, found in contact metamorphic limestones and dolostones.
facts.chrome-chalcedony: Chrome chalcedony is green chalcedony colored by chromium, a rock variety known from Western Australia and Zimbabwe.
facts.chrome-diopside: Chrome diopside is the chromium-rich variety of diopside, a pyroxene mineral.
facts.chromite: Chromite is an iron chromium oxide mineral and an ore of chromium, only cut as a curiosity.
facts.chrysocolla-chalcedony: Chrysocolla chalcedony is a rare blue to blue-green chalcedony, sold as Gem Silica and colored by copper.
facts.chrysoprase: A green, nickel-colored variety of chalcedony, a cryptocrystalline quartz.
facts.cinnabar: Cinnabar is a toxic mercury sulfide mineral and the main ore of mercury.
facts.citrine: The transparent, pale yellow to brownish orange variety of quartz.
facts.citron-chrysoprase: Citron chrysoprase is a nickel-bearing magnesite from Western Australia that is listed as a chrysoprase simulant.
facts.cleavelandite: Cleavelandite is a variety of albite that forms extremely thin, platy crystals, often found with tourmaline.
facts.clinochlore: Clinochlore is a mineral of the chlorite group, with several named varieties.
facts.clinozoisite: Clinozoisite is a monoclinic calcium aluminum silicate mineral of the epidote group, a rare transparent collectors mineral.
facts.cobaltite: Cobaltite is a rare sulfide mineral used mainly as an ore of cobalt.
facts.colemanite: Colemanite is a calcium borate mineral that forms in evaporite deposits and is a major ore of boron, rarely cut as a fragile gem.
facts.colombianite: Colombianite is a variety of obsidian from near Cali, Colombia, also called americanite.
facts.color-change-garnet: Color change garnet is any garnet that shifts color between daylight and incandescent light, not a single species.
facts.color-change-sapphire: Color change sapphire is sapphire whose color shifts between daylight or fluorescent light and incandescent light.
facts.columbite: Columbite is the niobium rich member of the columbite tantalite series and the main ore of niobium.
facts.conch-shell: Conch shell is the shell of the Queen conch, widely used for crafting and jewelry accessories.
facts.conichalcite: Conichalcite is a grass-green calcium copper arsenate hydroxide mineral that forms in the oxidation zone of copper ore bodies.
facts.copal: Copal is an amberlike resin that is typically softer than amber.
facts.copper-rutile: Copper rutile is copper-color rutile, traditionally seen as needle inclusions in quartz.
facts.coquimbite: Coquimbite is a mineral that forms as a secondary mineral in oxidized iron sulfide deposits in arid regions.
facts.coral: The skeletons of marine coral polyps, used as gem material.
facts.cordierite: Cordierite is a magnesium iron aluminum silicate mineral, and its gem quality form is called iolite.
facts.corundum: Corundum is an aluminum oxide mineral, most famous as the mineral of ruby and sapphire.
facts.covellite: Covellite is a copper mineral known for its strong metallic blue iridescence, prized by collectors.
facts.creedite: Creedite is an uncommon mineral found in fluorite-rich hydrothermal deposits and kept mostly as a collector stone.
facts.crocoite: Crocoite is a deep orange-red mineral that intrigues collectors, famous for its large crystals from Tasmania.
facts.cryolite: Cryolite is the ice stone, a soft mineral with a hardness of 2.5 that is now mostly made synthetically.
facts.cummingtonite: Cummingtonite is an amphibole mineral that forms a series with magnesio-cummingtonite and grunerite.
facts.cuprite: A type of copper oxide, mined as a copper ore and also forming as a patina on copper and bronze.
facts.cyanotrichite: Cyanotrichite is an uncommon blue copper mineral that forms radiating needle aggregates in the oxidation zone of copper deposits.
facts.dalmatian-jasper: A white to cream spotted decorative stone sold as jasper.
facts.dark-amber: Dark amber is a color form of amber.
facts.datolite: Datolite is a mineral that serves as a source of boron, with gems found more often in collections than in jewelry.
facts.demantoid-garnet: Demantoid is the green variety of andradite garnet, with colors from deep forest green to nearly colorless.
facts.dendritic-opal: Mineraloid (amorphous hydrated silica), not a crystalline mineral.
facts.dendritic-quartz: Dendritic quartz is transparent quartz with fern-like inclusions of iron, manganese or other metal oxides called dendrites.
facts.descloizite: Descloizite is a secondary mineral from the oxidized zone of base metal deposits that carry vanadium.
facts.desert-jasper: Desert Jasper is another sale name for polychrome jasper from Madagascar, named for its desert-like hues.
facts.desert-rose-selenite: Desert rose selenite is the well-known desert rose, gypsum in a rosette shape with sand inclusions.
facts.diamond: A rare, naturally occurring mineral made entirely of carbon, and the hardest known natural substance.
facts.diaspore: Diaspore is a mineral of the bauxite ore, and gem-grade color-changing crystals are cut from a Turkish deposit.
facts.diopside: Chrome diopside's deep green comes from chromium.
facts.dogtooth-calcite: Dogtooth calcite is the sharp, double-pyramid scalenohedral crystal form of calcite.
facts.dravite: Dravite is best known as the brown tourmaline, a relatively common member of the tourmaline group.
facts.eclogite: Eclogite is a metamorphic rock made mostly of garnet and a jadeitic pyroxene called omphacite.
facts.edenite: Edenite is a hornblende-group amphibole mineral named for Edenville, New York, found mostly in metamorphosed marble.
facts.ekanite: Ekanite is a rare gem mineral, often radioactive, named after its discoverer F. L. D. Ekanayake.
facts.emerald: The bluish green to green variety of beryl.
facts.enargite: Enargite is a copper arsenic sulfosalt mineral and an important ore of copper.
facts.enhydro-quartz: A trade term for transparent quartz holding a fluid inclusion, ideally with a gas bubble that moves when the stone is turned.
facts.enstatite: Enstatite is the magnesium silicate end of the orthopyroxene series, a pyroxene mineral that is lightly colored when pure.
facts.eosphorite: Eosphorite is the manganese member of a series with childrenite, typically a secondary mineral in phosphate-bearing granite pegmatites.
facts.epidote: A mineral species forming a solid-solution series with clinozoisite, within the epidote supergroup.
facts.erythrite: Erythrite is a deeply colored reddish or pink cobalt mineral, the cobalt member of a series with annabergite.
facts.ethiopian-opal: Welo opal formed as silica gel in porous volcanic rock lying on clay.
facts.ethiopian-welo-opal: Welo opal is opal from the Wollo Province of northern Ethiopia, often with vivid play-of-color, and much of it is hydrophane.
facts.euclase: A distinct mineral species, though it can form from the decomposition of beryl.
facts.eudialyte: A member of the eudialyte mineral group, a family of structurally related silicates.
facts.euxenite: Euxenite is a rare earth oxide mineral of granite pegmatites, a minor ore of rare earths and uranium.
facts.faden-quartz: Faden quartz is a descriptive term for tabular quartz crystals with a white thread-like zone running through the interior.
facts.fairy-stone: Fairy stone is a name for the twinned, often cross-shaped staurolite crystals found around Patrick County, Virginia.
facts.feldspar: Feldspar is a large group of rock-forming silicate minerals that includes the gem stones moonstone, sunstone, labradorite and amazonite.
facts.ferberite: Ferberite is the iron rich end member of the wolframite series and an important ore of tungsten.
facts.fire-agate: A brown agate that flashes iridescent yellow, red, orange and green from hemispherical surfaces.
facts.fire-opal: A red to yellow, translucent to transparent opal variety, usually faceted, named for its fire-like body color rather than play-of-color.
facts.fire-quartz: Colored crystalline quartz generally forms in pegmatites and veins from water solutions.
facts.flint: Flint is a variety of microcrystalline or cryptocrystalline quartz, a sedimentary rock.
facts.fluorite: A calcium fluoride mineral, important in industry, cut into gems and ornaments when color and clarity are good.
facts.franklinite: Franklinite is a black zinc iron manganese oxide mineral of the spinel group, found at Franklin, New Jersey.
facts.freshwater-pearl: Freshwater pearls are pearls formed by freshwater mussels, and are also called river pearls.
facts.fuchsite: Variety of muscovite in the mica group, not a separate species.
facts.fulgurite: Fulgurite is natural glass in tubes or crusts, formed when lightning fuses silica sand or rock.
facts.gabbro: Gabbro is a coarse-grained, dark-colored intrusive igneous rock made mainly of plagioclase and augite.
facts.gadolinite: Gadolinite is a rare yttrium and beryllium silicate mineral, mostly sought by collectors.
facts.galena: A lead sulfide mineral and the world's primary ore of lead, sometimes mined for its silver.
facts.garden-quartz: Colored crystalline quartz generally occurs in pegmatites and veins.
facts.garnet: A group of closely related rock-forming minerals, with gems in almost every color.
facts.garnierite: Garnierite is a nickel ore that rims dunite boulders and fills fractures and voids in nickel laterite deposits.
facts.gaspeite: Gaspeite is a rare nickel carbonate mineral and a member of the calcite mineral group.
facts.gem-silica: Gem silica is a bluish green to greenish blue variety of chalcedony colored by copper.
facts.gibbsite: Gibbsite is an aluminum hydroxide mineral and one of the three main minerals of the aluminum ore bauxite.
facts.girasol: Girasol opal is a semi-transparent to translucent opal with a moving, billowy light effect that resembles moonstone.
facts.glauberite: Glauberite is a mineral with the formula Na2Ca(SO4)2, found mainly in evaporite deposits.
facts.glaucophane: Glaucophane is a bluish mineral of metamorphic rocks and one of the components of blueschist.
facts.golden-hills-turquoise: Golden Hills turquoise is a turquoise from Kazakhstan, cut as a gem and set in rings with diamonds.
facts.goshenite: The colorless to near-colorless variety of beryl, also called white beryl.
facts.grape-agate: A marketing name for purple clusters of tiny quartz crystals shaped like bunches of grapes.
facts.gray-diamond: Gray diamond is a fancy colored diamond, one of the least appreciated fancy diamond colors.
facts.green-agate: Green agate is an agate with green color.
facts.green-amber: Green, blue or violet tints in amber are rare and come from extreme fluorescence.
facts.green-apatite: Green apatite is the green color of apatite, a calcium phosphate gem mineral, and it grows in large crystals.
facts.green-apophyllite: Green apophyllite is a pastel green color form of apophyllite, best known from Poona in India.
facts.green-beryl: Green beryl is a light green variety of beryl.
facts.green-diamond: Green diamond is a diamond whose color comes mostly from radiation damage to the crystal, and it is very rare.
facts.green-fluorite: Green is one color of fluorite, the mineral calcium fluoride (CaF2).
facts.green-garnet: Calcium garnets, including tsavorite and demantoid, typically form when limestone is altered to marble by contact metamorphism.
facts.green-jasper: Green jasper is jasper with a light to dark green color.
facts.green-kyanite: Green kyanite is the green color form of kyanite, an aluminum silicate gem mineral whose gems are mostly blue.
facts.green-malachite: Green malachite is malachite, a green copper carbonate hydroxide mineral prized as an ornamental stone.
facts.green-onyx: Onyx is a typically black-and-white banded variety of agate, a silicate mineral.
facts.green-opal: Prase opal's green is attributed to nickel-bearing inclusions.
facts.green-quartz: Green quartz is mostly prasiolite, a yellow-green to green quartz.
facts.green-sapphire: Green sapphire is a non-red corundum, so it counts as sapphire by definition.
facts.green-tiger-eye: Green tiger eye is tiger's-eye sold in a green color, which is usually produced by heat or dye treatment.
facts.green-tourmaline: Chromium or vanadium gives the intense green of chrome tourmaline.
facts.green-turquoise: Turquoise is a hydrated copper and aluminum phosphate, a mineral of the turquoise group.
facts.green-zircon: Zircon, a zirconium silicate mineral (family statement).
facts.greenlandite: Greenlandite is a green to bluish green quartzite colored by fuchsite mica, from the Nuuk area of Greenland.
facts.greenockite: Greenockite is a rare cadmium sulfide mineral and the only cadmium mineral of importance.
facts.gypsum: Gypsum is an evaporite mineral and the most common sulfate mineral, found in layered sedimentary deposits.
facts.gyrolite: Gyrolite is a mineral that forms spherical to radial masses in vugs and veinlets of basalts, named from the Greek for round.
facts.halite: The mineral form of common salt, sodium chloride.
facts.hambergite: Hambergite is an uncommon accessory mineral of granite pegmatites, mostly seen in collections.
facts.hanksite: Hanksite is a sodium potassium sulfate carbonate mineral that forms in lake evaporite deposits.
facts.hauyne: Haüyne is a rare blue sodalite-group mineral, related to lazurite and part of lapis lazuli, that is only rarely faceted.
facts.hawks-eye: Hawks Eye is the unstained blue form of tigers eye, quartz that replaced fibrous crocidolite.
facts.hedenbergite: Hedenbergite is a pyroxene group mineral that forms a series with diopside.
facts.heliodor: A yellow, greenish yellow or golden-yellow variety of the mineral beryl.
facts.hemimorphite: A zinc silicate mineral and a minor ore of zinc, common as a secondary mineral in weathered rock above zinc deposits.
facts.herderite: Herderite is a rare calcium beryllium phosphate mineral, the fluorine-rich end member of a series with hydroxylherderite.
facts.herkimer-diamond: Doubly terminated quartz crystals found in Herkimer County, New York, not true diamond.
facts.hessonite: Orange to cinnamon variety of grossular garnet, the calcium-aluminum member of the garnet group.
facts.heulandite: Heulandite is one of the more common zeolite minerals, with a distinctive crystal form and a pearly luster on cleavage surfaces.
facts.hexagonite: Hexagonite is the pinkish purple variety of tremolite, a rare gem that owes its color to manganese.
facts.hiddenite: Hiddenite is the green, chromium-rich transparent variety of spodumene first found in North Carolina.
facts.hollandite: Hollandite is an opaque manganese-ore mineral of the cryptomelane group, found in metamorphic manganese ores.
facts.holly-blue-agate: Holly Blue is a lavender-toned blue chalcedony from Oregon, arguably the most valuable type of blue chalcedony.
facts.honey-calcite: A yellow to honey-colored form of calcite.
facts.hornblende: Hornblende is a field and classroom name for a group of dark-colored amphibole minerals found in many igneous and metamorphic rocks.
facts.howlite: The dark veins are black, threadlike impurities or host-rock matrix the howlite grows around.
facts.humite: Humite is the namesake mineral of the humite group, a magnesium iron silicate with fluorine and hydroxyl.
facts.hurlbutite: Hurlbutite is a rare calcium beryllium phosphate mineral that forms late in granite pegmatites.
facts.hydrogrossular-garnet: Hydrogrossular is a garnet that is never transparent and is often used as a jade substitute.
facts.hypersthene: Hypersthene is an orthopyroxene, an iron-magnesium silicate between enstatite and ferrosilite, that is sometimes used as an ornamental stone.
facts.iceland-spar: Iceland spar is clear, cleaved, colorless calcite, best known for showing double refraction.
facts.ilmenite: Ilmenite is a black iron-titanium oxide mineral and the primary ore of titanium.
facts.impactite: Impactite is terrestrial rock altered by the heat, pressure and shock of a large meteorite impact.
facts.imperial-jasper: Imperial jasper is a Mexican jasper variegated in green and yellow, partly translucent, and priced at a premium because it is relatively rare.
facts.imperial-topaz: A prized color variety of topaz, reddish orange to orangy red.
facts.indonesian-blue-amber: Indonesian blue amber is a rare blue amber with some production from Indonesia, where its blue is a UV fluorescence.
facts.inesite: Inesite is an uncommon pink manganese-bearing mineral that collectors prize for its chisel-shaped crystals.
facts.jade: A cultural term for a very durable material used for tools, carvings and gems, covering two different minerals, jadeite and nephrite.
facts.jamesonite: Jamesonite is a hydrothermal lead antimony sulfide mineral with the formula Pb4FeSb6S14.
facts.japan-law-twin: Japan Law Twin is a twinning form of quartz in which two crystals are joined.
facts.jasper: An opaque, solid or patterned variety of cryptocrystalline quartz colored by mineral impurities.
facts.jaspillite: Jaspillite, spelled jaspilite in the source, is a banded iron formation rock of gray hematite and red jasper bands.
facts.jeremejevite: Jeremejevite is a rare borate mineral, best known for its aesthetic blue and gemmy crystals.
facts.jet: Black organic gem material, a variety of lignite coal that forms from fossilized wood.
facts.k2-jasper: K2 Jasper is a white granite from northern Pakistan with blue azurite orbs, and it is not jasper.
facts.kammererite: A chromium-bearing variety of clinochlore, a mineral in the chlorite group.
facts.kernite: Kernite is a sodium borate mineral first found in 1926 at Boron, California, and a key source of borax.
facts.kimberlite: Kimberlite is an igneous rock known as the main host rock of diamonds, named for Kimberley in South Africa.
facts.kingman-turquoise: Variety of the mineral turquoise, an opaque hydrous copper aluminum phosphate.
facts.kinoite: Kinoite is a monoclinic calcium copper silicate hydroxide mineral with a deep azurite-blue color.
facts.kornerupine: Kornerupine is a rare magnesium aluminum boron silicate mineral that is cut as a gemstone, usually dark brown or green.
facts.kunzite: The best-known variety of the mineral spodumene, named after George F. Kunz.
facts.kyanite: Orange kyanite from Loliondo, Tanzania owes its color to small amounts of manganese.
facts.labradorite: A plagioclase feldspar, best known for the iridescent flash called labradorescence.
facts.lace-agate: A variety of agate, which is chalcedony (microcrystalline quartz).
facts.lapis-lazuli: A blue rock made of several minerals, mainly lazurite with calcite and pyrite, prized since antiquity.
facts.lawsonite: Lawsonite is a rare mineral described as a hydrated variant of the feldspar anorthite.
facts.lazulite: Lazulite is an aesthetic blue mineral that forms in distinct crystals.
facts.legrandite: Legrandite is an uncommon zinc arsenate mineral that forms in the oxidized zone of zinc and arsenic deposits.
facts.lepidolite: A rare lithium-rich mica mineral, usually pink, red or purple.
facts.leucite: Leucite is a feldspathoid mineral that forms directly from cooling lava in volcanic rock.
facts.libethenite: Libethenite is an uncommon secondary mineral that forms in the oxidized zone of copper deposits.
facts.limonite: Limonite is a mineraloid of hydrous iron oxides, not a true mineral, formed mostly by the weathering of iron-bearing materials.
facts.linarite: Linarite is a very rare blue collector mineral that forms as a secondary mineral in the oxidized zones of lead-copper deposits.
facts.lizardite: Lizardite is a mineral of the kaolinite serpentine group, probably the most common serpentine mineral.
facts.lodestone: Lodestone is a naturally magnetized form of magnetite that can pick up small pieces of iron.
facts.loellingite: Loellingite is an uncommon arsenic mineral of the Loellingite group, found in veins with other sulfides.
facts.ludlamite: Ludlamite is an iron magnesium manganese phosphate mineral found in granite pegmatites.
facts.magnetite: A very common iron oxide mineral, found in igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks, and the most commonly mined ore of iron.
facts.mahogany-obsidian: A reddish-brown to black variety of obsidian, which is natural volcanic glass formed from rapidly cooled lava.
facts.malachite: A green copper carbonate hydroxide mineral and a minor copper ore, often cut into cabochons, beads and carvings.
facts.mali-garnet: Mali garnet is a yellow-green to brown gem garnet from Mali with a composition between grossular and andradite.
facts.mammoth-ivory: Organic gem material cut from the tusks of the extinct mammoth.
facts.mandarin-garnet: Mandarin garnet is a trade name for vivid orange spessartite garnet, first found in Namibia.
facts.maw-sit-sit: Maw sit sit is a chromium-rich metamorphic rock with bright green color and black or white spots, bands and swirls, and it is not a true jade.
facts.mellite: Mellite is an uncommon secondary mineral that forms in brown coal and lignite deposits.
facts.mesolite: Mesolite is a zeolite group mineral found in cavities of volcanic rocks, typically basalt, and in hydrothermal veins.
facts.mexican-agate: Mexican agate is a name for agate from Mexico, and rarely a misnomer for Mexican onyx, which is a banded travertine.
facts.mexican-fire-opal: A red to yellow, translucent to transparent opal variety, usually faceted, named for its fire-like body color rather than play-of-color.
facts.microcline: Microcline is a potassium feldspar polymorphous with orthoclase and sanidine, differing from them only in crystal structure.
facts.microlite: Microlite is a tantalum-rich member of the pyrochlore supergroup, found as small crystals and rarely cut as gems.
facts.milky-quartz: Forms in crystalline quartz veins and pegmatites, often with gold in hydrothermal veins.
facts.millerite: Millerite is a nickel ore mineral known for slender brassy crystals and hair-like tufts.
facts.mimetite: Mimetite is a mineral of the apatite group, found in many places around the world.
facts.mohawkite: Mohawkite is a mixture of copper arsenide minerals, copper and silver found at the Mohawk Mine in Michigan.
facts.moldavite: A natural glass thought to have formed in an asteroid impact about 15 million years ago.
facts.monazite: Monazite is a rare phosphate mineral mined from placer deposits for its rare earth and thorium content.
facts.mookaite-jasper: Silicified porcelanite, classed as a rock.
facts.moonstone: Gem-quality feldspar showing adularescence, a soft glow that seems to float under the surface.
facts.moqui-marbles: Small brownish-black balls of iron oxide and sandstone that weather out of Navajo Sandstone.
facts.mordenite: Mordenite is a zeolite mineral that forms in veins in igneous rocks and from volcanic glass, with fibrous material sometimes cut for collectors.
facts.morganite: The pink to orange-pink variety of beryl, the mineral species that also includes emerald and aquamarine.
facts.moroccan-agate: Moroccan agate is agate from deposits in the Atlas Mountains, with Sidi Rahal the best studied source.
facts.mottramite: Mottramite is a secondary mineral from the oxidized zone of base metal deposits that carry vanadium.
facts.muscovite: Muscovite is the most common mineral of the mica family and a major rock-forming mineral.
facts.natrolite: A mineral species in the zeolite group.
facts.neon-apatite: Neon apatite is bright green to blue gem apatite from southern Madagascar whose neon color comes from heat treatment.
facts.nepheline: Nepheline is a rock-forming mineral found mostly in alkali-rich igneous rocks, and it is rarely cut as a gem.
facts.neptunite: Neptunite is a relatively recent mineral first found in the early 1900s, with black crystals often on white natrolite.
facts.nontronite: Nontronite is a soft, claylike mineral of the smectite group, formed as a weathering product of basalts.
facts.obsidian: An igneous rock and a mineraloid, not a mineral.
facts.ocean-jasper: A silicified rhyolite sold as a variety of orbicular jasper.
facts.okenite: Okenite is a hydrated calcium silicate mineral that often forms white cotton-ball clusters of very fine fibers in volcanic cavities.
facts.oligoclase: Oligoclase is a plagioclase feldspar, treated by the IMA as a calcium-rich variety of albite.
facts.opal: A hydrated, amorphous form of silica, chemically like quartz but with 3% to 21% water.
facts.orange-aventurine: Orange aventurine is sparkly translucent quartz or quartzite whose orange color can come from hematite or goethite inclusions.
facts.orange-diamond: Orange diamond is a diamond with an orange body color, caused mostly by nitrogen impurities in the crystal.
facts.orange-kyanite: Orange kyanite is kyanite in a rare orange color, shown here from Tanzania.
facts.orange-sapphire: Orange sapphire is a fancy sapphire, meaning a gem-quality corundum in a color other than red.
facts.orbicular-jasper: Jasper is colored by various mineral impurities.
facts.oregon-sunstone: Oregon sunstone is a labradorite feldspar from Oregon whose copper inclusions can give a schiller glow.
facts.orpiment: Orpiment is a mineral known for its strikingly bright yellow color, though it can also be bright orange or lustrous brown.
facts.orthoclase: A feldspar mineral with formula KAlSi3O8.
facts.owyhee-blue-opal: Owyhee Blue Opal is blue opal mined in the Owyhee Mountains of eastern Oregon near the Idaho border.
facts.padparadscha-sapphire: Padparadscha sapphire is a variety of corundum with a subtle pinkish orange to orangey pink color.
facts.painite: Painite is a rare gem mineral found only in Myanmar, first identified as a new species in 1957.
facts.papagoite: Papagoite is a rare gem material first found in Ajo, Arizona, and also found in South Africa and Namibia.
facts.paragonite: Paragonite is a mineral of the mica group that occurs in low- to medium-grade metamorphic schists and phyllites.
facts.pargasite: Pargasite is a calcic amphibole mineral of the hornblende group, named after Pargas in Finland.
facts.peach-moonstone: A peach-colored moonstone, a warm-toned feldspar with adularescent sheen.
facts.peach-quartz: Peach quartz is a name some people give to orange quartz, a quartz colored by impurities.
facts.peacock-ore: Peacock ore is the name for bornite, a copper iron sulfide mineral, called that for its tarnish.
facts.peanut-obsidian: Peanut obsidian is a gray to greenish gray perlite with red stellate spherulites that look like a mass of peanuts.
facts.peanut-wood: Peanut wood is a petrified wood from Australia, dark brown to black with white markings the size of a peanut.
facts.pegmatite: Pegmatite is an igneous rock made almost entirely of crystals more than one centimeter across.
facts.peridot: The green gem variety of the mineral olivine, found in mantle rock, lava and meteorites.
facts.peristerite: Peristerite is primarily oligoclase with a complex mixture of feldspars, and it shows a blue or white iridescence.
facts.persian-turquoise: A color and trade name for the finest sky-blue turquoise, long associated with Iranian mines.
facts.perthite: Perthite is an intergrowth of feldspars, albite and oligoclase with orthoclase or microcline.
facts.petalite: Petalite is a lithium bearing mineral that rarely occurs as gem quality crystal and suits earrings and pendants.
facts.petrified-wood: Fossilized wood where plant tissue has been replaced by minerals, mostly silica.
facts.pezzottaite: Pezzottaite is a rare mineral similar to beryl that is recognized as its own species and sometimes sold as raspberry beryl.
facts.phantom-quartz: A rock crystal containing ghost-like inner outlines of earlier crystal faces, formed when growth paused and other minerals coated the faces.
facts.phosphophyllite: Phosphophyllite is a rare zinc phosphate mineral that can show a lovely blue-green color.
facts.picture-jasper: A jasper variety whose patterns look like scenes or pictures when cut.
facts.pink-amethyst: Amethyst is a violet variety of quartz, so pink amethyst would be a light amethyst within quartz.
facts.pink-aventurine: Pink aventurine is aventurine quartz whose pink color and sparkle come from tiny flakes of lepidolite mica.
facts.pink-diamond: Pink diamond is a fancy colored diamond, among the rarest gems on the planet.
facts.pink-grossular-garnet: Pink grossular garnet is the light pink to raspberry-red form of grossular, a member of the garnet group.
facts.pink-halite: Pink halite is pink-colored halite, found for example as hopper crystals at Searles Lake in California.
facts.pink-jade: Pink jade is a name sometimes given to Wyoming jade that gets its color from thulite, a variety of zoisite.
facts.pink-opal: A pink variety of common opal, opal without play-of-color.
facts.pink-sapphire: Sapphire is corundum in every color except red.
facts.pink-topaz: Chromium causes pink and red color in topaz.
facts.pipestone: Pipestone is a soft red claystone (argillite) called catlinite that has long been quarried to make pipes.
facts.plumbogummite: Plumbogummite is an uncommon secondary mineral of the crandallite group, found in oxidized lead deposits.
facts.plume-agate: Plume agate is a kind of moss agate, mostly pale agate holding fluffy red, yellow or violet masses that resemble egret plumes.
facts.pollucite: Pollucite is a rare cesium zeolite mineral and the main ore of cesium, only occasionally cut as a gem.
facts.polychrome-jasper: A descriptive name for jasper showing several colors.
facts.porcelain-jasper: Porcelain jasper is a hard, naturally baked impure clay, or porcellanite, whose red color makes it look like jasper.
facts.powellite: Powellite is a rare calcium molybdate mineral that forms a series with scheelite and is mostly a collectors mineral.
facts.prasiolite: A yellow-green to green variety of quartz, cut as faceted stones for jewelry or collectors.
facts.prehnite: A calcium aluminum silicate mineral, popular as a green cabochon material and sometimes faceted.
facts.prehnite-epidote: Prehnite is most often a vein or amygdule mineral in basalt, associated with native copper, laumontite, epidote, chlorite, quartz and calcite.
facts.preseli-bluestone: Preseli Bluestone is a spotted metamorphosed dolerite from the Preseli Hills in Wales.
facts.proustite: Proustite is a deep red silver arsenic sulfide mineral, a rare collector gem that was also a minor silver ore.
facts.pumpellyite: Pumpellyite is a group of closely related minerals found in igneous and metamorphic rocks, named for geologist Raphael Pumpelly.
facts.purple-apatite: Purple apatite is the violet to purple color of apatite, a phosphate mineral, and is highly prized.
facts.purple-chalcedony: Purple chalcedony is a microcrystalline form of amethyst quartz with a grayish, slightly reddish purple color.
facts.purple-diamond: Purple diamonds are fancy-colored diamonds colored by natural plastic deformation, and pure purple stones are very rare.
facts.purple-fluorite: Purple fluorite is fluorite, the mineral calcium fluoride, in purple color.
facts.purple-jade: A purple rock containing jadeite and quartz, reported from Turkey and now used in the jewelry trade for beads, cabochons and carvings.
facts.purple-scapolite: Purple scapolite is the purple gem color of scapolite, the second most common gem color after yellow.
facts.purpurite: Rare manganese-dominant end member of a mineral series with heterosite, a purple manganese iron phosphate.
facts.pyrargyrite: Pyrargyrite is a silver-bearing mineral of the proustite group, rarely cut as a gem.
facts.pyrite: A brass-yellow iron sulfide mineral with a bright metallic luster, the most common sulfide mineral.
facts.pyromorphite: A lead chlorophosphate mineral of the apatite group, sometimes mined as an ore of lead.
facts.pyrope: Pyrope is a member of the garnet group and makes a popular dark red gemstone.
facts.pyrophyllite: Pyrophyllite is a soft aluminum silicate mineral like talc, used for ceramics and as a minor carving stone.
facts.pyroxmangite: Pyroxmangite is a rare manganese silicate mineral and a high-temperature polymorph of rhodonite.
facts.pyrrhotite: Pyrrhotite is a magnetic iron sulfide mineral with a bronze color.
facts.quartz: Quartz is a mineral made of silicon and oxygen, the most abundant mineral in Earth's crust.
facts.quartz-geode: A geode is a rock structure, not a mineral species.
facts.quartzite: Quartzite is a nonfoliated metamorphic rock made almost entirely of quartz, formed when quartz-rich sandstone is altered.
facts.rainbow-andradite-garnet: Rainbow andradite garnet is a rare dark root-beer-brown andradite garnet that shows an iridescent phenomenon.
facts.rainbow-fluorite: A multi-colored fluorite cut from color-zoned crystals.
facts.rainbow-lattice-sunstone: A rare sunstone from Australia that shows glitter, a bluish glow and a rainbow lattice pattern.
facts.rainbow-moonstone: A trade name mostly used for white labradorite, a plagioclase feldspar with blue flashes.
facts.rainbow-obsidian: A variety of obsidian with a multicolored, iridescent sheen from inclusions.
facts.rainforest-jasper: Rhyolite, an extrusive igneous rock formed from silica-rich magma that cools quickly on the surface.
facts.realgar: An arsenic sulfide mineral and one of the principal sources of arsenic.
facts.red-agate: Red agate is an agate with red color, from iron oxide bands.
facts.red-beryl: An extremely rare red variety of beryl colored by trace manganese.
facts.red-diamond: Red diamond is a fancy-colored diamond with a red hue, the rarest of all the fancy-colored diamond varieties.
facts.red-jade: Jade is an umbrella term for two rocks, jadeite (sodium aluminum pyroxene) and nephrite (calcium magnesium amphibole).
facts.red-spinel: Red spinel is the red color of spinel, a gem species from a group of related minerals.
facts.rhodizite: Rhodizite is a rare late-stage mineral of alkali-rich granite pegmatites and the potassium end member of a series with londonite.
facts.rhodochrosite: A manganese carbonate mineral from light pink to bright red, used as a manganese ore, gemstone and specimen.
facts.rhodonite: A pink manganese silicate mineral of variable composition, used as a gem and ornamental stone.
facts.rhyolite: Rhyolite is an extrusive igneous rock with a very high silica content, usually pink or gray with very fine grains.
facts.richterite: Richterite is a sodic-calcic amphibole mineral named for the German mineralogist Theodor Richter.
facts.roman-glass: Glass made and worked in the Roman world, used for tablewares, toilet items, jewelry, storage, mosaics and more.
facts.rosasite: Rosasite is an uncommon copper zinc carbonate mineral that forms in the oxidized zone of copper and zinc deposits.
facts.rose-quartz: A pink variety of quartz, usually translucent and massive rather than in clear crystals.
facts.rubellite: Dark pink to red variety of tourmaline, colored by trace manganese.
facts.ruby: A variety of the mineral species corundum (aluminum oxide).
facts.ruby-fuchsite: Bright red corundum (ruby) crystals found inside green fuchsite mica, sold as a mixed gem material.
facts.rudraksha: The cleaned stone (pit or seed) of the fruit of Elaeocarpus trees, used as Hindu prayer beads.
facts.rutilated-quartz: A variety of quartz, a mineral made of silicon and oxygen.
facts.rutile: Rutile is a titanium oxide mineral, TiO2, known for its bright luster and its needles inside other gems.
facts.saltwater-pearl: Saltwater pearls are pearls grown in marine oysters, natural or cultured, and they set the traditional standard for the round white pearl.
facts.samarskite: Samarskite is a radioactive, brittle, metamict yttrium niobium tantalum oxide mineral found in granite pegmatites.
facts.sanidine: Sanidine is a potassium feldspar mineral of volcanic rocks, with little gem significance.
facts.sapphire: Gem-quality corundum of any color except red (red is ruby).
facts.sapphirine: Sapphirine is a rare gem mineral species distinct from sapphire, most often grayish blue.
facts.sardonyx: A banded chalcedony with red to brown (sard) bands alternating with black or white (onyx) bands.
facts.satin-spar: Satin spar is a fibrous variety of gypsum that shows a chatoyant glow when cut as cabochons.
facts.saussurite: Saussurite is an alteration product of basaltic rocks, mostly albite and epidote or zoisite, sometimes sold as jade.
facts.scapolite: Scapolite is a mineral group with a series from marialite to meionite, and the gems that form in it carry the name.
facts.schalenblende: Schalenblende is a banded zinc sulfide rock of sphalerite, sometimes layered with wurtzite, and rarely cut into cabochons.
facts.scheelite: A calcium tungstate mineral and an important ore of tungsten.
facts.scorodite: Scorodite is a secondary mineral of the variscite group, formed by oxidation of sulfides that contain arsenic.
facts.septarian-nodule: Septarian nodules, also called septaria, are concretions with radial and concentric septa of coarse minerals.
facts.serandite: Serandite is a rare mineral, the manganese end member of a series with pectolite, famous from Mont Saint Hilaire in Quebec.
facts.shaman-stone: Shaman stone is a collector name for Moqui marbles, iron concretions of iron oxide and sandstone.
facts.shark-tooth: Shark teeth are very hard structures of enameloid over dentine, and fossil ones take their color from the sediment.
facts.siderite: Carbonate mineral of the calcite group, forming solid-solution series with magnesite, rhodochrosite and smithsonite.
facts.sillimanite: Sillimanite is a metamorphic aluminum silicate mineral, trimorphous with kyanite and andalusite and cut as a rare collector gem.
facts.silver-rutile: Silver rutile here means silvery gray tufts of the titanium dioxide mineral rutile, found inside quartz crystals.
facts.silver-sheen-obsidian: A sheen variety of obsidian (volcanic glass) with a silvery light effect.
facts.sinhalite: Sinhalite is a rare mineral formed in boron-rich skarns and found as gem pebbles in Sri Lanka.
facts.sleeping-beauty-turquoise: Sleeping Beauty turquoise is turquoise from the Sleeping Beauty mine in Globe, Arizona, prized for its even sky blue color.
facts.smithsonite: Smithsonite is a zinc carbonate mineral, an ore of zinc and a minor gemstone.
facts.smoky-quartz: A brown to black color variety of the mineral quartz.
facts.snow-quartz: A milky white, cloudy variety of quartz, the same material as milky quartz.
facts.snowflake-obsidian: A black variety of obsidian (volcanic glass) with white snowflake-like inclusions of cristobalite, the mineral that crystallizes inside the glass.
facts.sodalite: A blue to blue-violet feldspathoid mineral used as gem, carving and architectural stone.
facts.sonora-sunrise: Sonora Sunrise is a trade name for a rock made mainly of bluish-green chrysocolla and bright red cuprite.
facts.sonora-sunset: Sonora Sunset is a trade name for a rock of bluish-green chrysocolla and bright red cuprite.
facts.spectrolite: Spectrolite is a trade name for labradorite feldspar from Finland that shows strong flashes of several colors.
facts.sphalerite: A zinc sulfide mineral and the most important ore of zinc.
facts.sphene-titanite: Sphene Titanite is a rare titanium mineral, called titanite by geologists and sphene as a gemstone.
facts.spinel: The magnesium-aluminium member of the spinel mineral group, long mistaken for ruby.
facts.spodumene: Spodumene is a pyroxene mineral found in lithium-rich pegmatites, with kunzite, hiddenite and triphane as its gem colors.
facts.sponge-coral: Sponge coral is the trade name of Melithaea ochracea, a gem coral from the South China Sea with open, sponge-like holes.
facts.spurrite: Spurrite is a mineral formed by high-temperature thermal metamorphism along the contact between carbonate rock and mafic magma.
facts.star-garnet: The star comes from oriented rutile needle inclusions.
facts.star-ruby: Ruby (red corundum) cut as a cabochon to show a six-rayed star from rutile needle inclusions.
facts.star-sapphire: A sapphire that shows a star-like effect called asterism, caused by intersecting needle-like inclusions.
facts.staurolite: Staurolite is a metamorphic mineral famous for its twinned, cross-shaped crystals, found in schist and gneiss.
facts.steatite-soapstone: Steatite Soapstone is a rock made up largely or wholly of the mineral talc.
facts.stibnite: Stibnite is the primary ore of antimony and forms some of the most outstanding natural crystals.
facts.stromatolite: Stromatolites are hard, raised, reef-like structures built by cyanobacteria.
facts.strontianite: Strontianite is a strontium carbonate mineral and, with celestine, a principal ore of strontium.
facts.sugilite: A rare pink to purple gemstone and silicate mineral.
facts.sunset-tourmaline: Sunset tourmaline is a bicolor form of tourmaline cut as a gem and set in jewelry such as rings.
facts.sunstone: Feldspar with tiny reflective inclusions that give a glittery flash called aventurescence.
facts.tantalite: Tantalite is a dark, very heavy oxide mineral, the tantalum rich member of a series with columbite and an important ore.
facts.tanzanite: The blue-violet variety of zoisite, named by Tiffany & Co after Tanzania.
facts.thulite: Thulite is the pink to reddish variety of the mineral zoisite, an opaque stone used as a minor gemstone.
facts.thunder-bay-amethyst: Thunder Bay amethyst is amethyst from vein deposits around Thunder Bay, where gem quality material is extremely rare.
facts.tiffany-stone: A trade name for a purple, blue and white gem material from Utah, cut into beads, cabochons and tumbled stones.
facts.tiger-iron: Tiger iron is a market name for a red, hematite-rich microcrystalline quartz rock from banded iron formations in Western Australia.
facts.tigers-eye: Chatoyant quartz-group material formed when blue crocidolite alters to quartz with fibrous structure kept, then iron-stained golden brown.
facts.topaz: A silicate mineral containing aluminum and fluorine, hardness 8, sold in many natural and treated colors.
facts.tourmaline: A supergroup of boron silicate minerals with over thirty species, occurring in more colors than any other mineral group.
facts.tremolite: Tremolite is a mineral that forms a series with actinolite, and its dense fibrous form is nephrite jade.
facts.triphane: Triphane is the name for yellow gem-quality spodumene, and an early name for spodumene itself.
facts.triplite: Triplite is a manganese iron phosphate mineral found mainly in granite pegmatites.
facts.tsavorite-garnet: Tsavorite is a bright green grossular garnet, one of the two calcium garnets highly regarded in the gem trade.
facts.tugtupite: Tugtupite is a rare gem mineral of the helvine group, first discovered in 1960 and closely related to sodalite.
facts.turquoise: An opaque mineral in shades of blue, bluish green, green and yellowish green, treasured as a gemstone for thousands of years.
facts.turritella-agate: A brown, translucent to semi-transparent fossil-bearing agate from the Green River Formation of Wyoming, full of spiral snail shells.
facts.umbalite: Umbalite is a trade name for a garnet, either malaya garnet or rhodolite from the Umba valley.
facts.unakite: A pink and green metamorphic rock, popular as lapidary material.
facts.uvarovite: Uvarovite is a rare member of the garnet group that is always deep green in color.
facts.uvite: Uvite is an uncommon tourmaline named for the Uva Province of Sri Lanka, where it was first identified.
facts.variscite: A rare hydrated aluminum phosphate mineral, usually green, often cut into cabochons and small carvings.
facts.vayrynenite: Vayrynenite is a mineral that forms as an alteration product of beryl and triphylite in complex zoned granite pegmatites.
facts.vera-cruz-amethyst: Vera Cruz amethyst is amethyst from Vera Cruz in Mexico, noted for very pale, clear prismatic crystals.
facts.verdite: Verdite is a trade name for grayish green to bright green metamorphic rocks colored by fuchsite mica.
facts.vesuvianite: A calcium aluminum silicate mineral, also known as idocrase, especially when used as a gem.
facts.veszelyite: Veszelyite is a rare copper zinc phosphate mineral found in the oxidized zone of some base-metal deposits.
facts.villiaumite: Villiaumite is a sodium fluoride mineral found in nepheline syenite and its pegmatites.
facts.violet-sapphire: Corundum (family statement, all gem-quality corundum other than red is sapphire).
facts.vivianite: Mineral species in the vivianite group.
facts.watermelon-tourmaline: A concentrically color-zoned elbaite variety of tourmaline.
facts.wavellite: Wavellite is a radiating phosphate mineral that forms pinwheel balls, named after William Wavell.
facts.whewellite: Whewellite is a rare oxalate mineral that forms in veins, coal seams and organic concretions, best kept as a display piece.
facts.white-agate: Agate is a banded variety of chalcedony, a fibrous form of quartz.
facts.white-buffalo-stone: White buffalo stone is a name for a white cabochon material described as a so-to-speak albino turquoise.
facts.white-calcite: White is the usual color of calcite, a carbonate mineral.
facts.white-jade: White nephrite is found in small quarries and as river pebbles and boulders near the Kuen-Lun range.
facts.white-opal: Play of color in opal comes from diffraction by stacked silica spheres and is unrelated to body color.
facts.white-topaz: White topaz is colorless topaz, a gem variety of the topaz mineral.
facts.white-turquoise: Turquoise is an opaque mineral, a hydrous copper and aluminum phosphate.
facts.willemite: A zinc silicate mineral, the zinc analogue of phenakite.
facts.wolframite: Wolframite is a series of iron manganese tungstate minerals between huebnerite and ferberite, and an important ore of tungsten.
facts.wollastonite: Wollastonite is a calcium silicate mineral that is an important industrial material and is sometimes cut as a curiosity gem.
facts.xonotlite: Xonotlite is a mineral that forms in contact metamorphic deposits within limestones, serpentinites and metavolcanic rocks.
facts.yellow-agate: Agate forms when silica from groundwater fills cavities, and color bands come from changing water chemistry.
facts.yellow-apatite: Apatite is a group of phosphate minerals, not one species.
facts.yellow-aventurine: A yellow color of aventurine, a translucent quartz or quartzite with sparkly mineral inclusions (aventurescence).
facts.yellow-diamond: Yellow diamond is a fancy colored diamond whose yellow most often comes from nitrogen impurities in the crystal lattice.
facts.yellow-jade: Jadeite color is caused by impurities.
facts.yellow-opal: Opal forms when water deposits microscopic silica spheres in rock cavities, as silica gel fills crevices.
facts.yellow-quartz: Yellow quartz is the yellow to orange variety of quartz that is known as citrine.
facts.yellow-sapphire: Sapphire is a variety of the mineral corundum.
facts.yellow-topaz: Yellow topaz is the yellow form of topaz, which is a naturally occurring neo-silicate mineral.
facts.zebra-stone: Zebra stone, also called zebra rock, is a banded siliceous argillite known only from Western Australia.
facts.zincite: Zincite is a rare zinc oxide mineral with a distinctive bright orange color.
facts.zircon: A zirconium silicate mineral, used as a gemstone for about 2000 years and today the primary ore of zirconium.
facts.zunyite: Zunyite is a mineral that forms cubic, tetrahedral crystals in highly aluminous shales and altered volcanic rocks.
